local_question: When the world's own writing begins to carry the measurable statistical signature of the models trained on it — Kobak et al.'s excess-vocabulary shift as the concrete instance — the field's whole literature on avoiding collapse rests on one remedy: keep fresh real data in the loop. That remedy assumes the injected 'real data' is outside the loop. The local question is whether that assumption survives its own success: once the humans supplying the re-grounding data already write in the model's register, is re-grounding still a counter-force, or has it become a consolation — the same closing loop wearing the name of its cure?
method_or_operation: Source-reading and the practice's own prior findings used as instruments — no generation whose provenance is the subject, no new external cost. The practice's founding method is error-made-legible; model collapse is its inverse, error (the margin, the tail, the outlier) made silently invisible. The compose gate stays (§5.4 non-replaceability): not a dashboard, not a decorated thesis; the default output is a research note, or a negative result.
first_move: Read Kobak, D. et al., 'Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary' (Science Advances 2024; arXiv:2406.07016) at the primary — one full-text extraction budgeted, load-bearing. Extract, verbatim where it carries weight: (a) exactly what is measured against what control; (b) whether the paper documents the outlier/margin dissolving or only frequency shifts of common style-words; (c) whether it speaks to re-grounding at all. Then judge whether the 're-grounding as consolation' thesis has a measurable anchor in this present or is, at present, conjecture — and mark it as whichever it is.
